cards.lore: Recognizes PAMPs (microbes, e.g., flagellin via TLR5) and DAMPs (sterile danger signals). Triggers NF-kB signaling to initiate pro-inflammatory cytokine production.
Arrives first via IL-8. Uses NADPH oxidase to make superoxide (HOCl). CGD patients lack this enzyme, suffering recurrent catalase-positive infections.
M1 (IFN-γ-activated): kills pathogens with ROS, M2 (IL-4/IL-13-activated): promotes healing and fibrosis. Presents antigens on MHC II to CD4+ T cells.
The most powerful APC. Can uniquely present exogenous viral antigens on MHC I to prime naive CD8+ T cells in the lymph node.
Kills virally infected or tumor cells that downregulate MHC I to hide from T cells. Uses perforin/granzyme. Performs ADCC via CD16.
Classical, Lectin, and Alternative pathways converge on C3b opsonization and C5b-9 (MAC lysis). Regulated by CD55 (DAF) and CD59.
The alarm signals. C3a strongly attracts neutrophils and triggers mast cells. In sepsis, massive C5a causes simultaneous inflammation and neutrophil immunosuppression.
Triggered by viral nucleic acids. Signals via JAK-STAT to upregulate PKR (blocks viral translation) and increase MHC I expression on adjacent cells.
Vasodilation (histamine) → Permeability (bradykinin) → Diapedesis (selectins/integrins). Resolves via IL-10/TGF-β or progresses to chronic fibrosis.
Built by macrophages + Th1 cells (IFN-γ) when acute clearance fails. Anti-TNF therapy (infliximab) destroys the wall, risking fatal reactivation of latent Tb.
Signal 1 = TCR + MHC. Signal 2 = Co-stimulation (CD28 + CD80/86). Without Signal 2, the T cell enters anergy (permanent shutdown).
Fights intracellular pathogens. Secretes IFN-γ to supercharge macrophages and upregulate MHC II. Drives delayed-type hypersensitivity and autoimmune tissue damage.
Driven by IL-4. Secretes IL-4 (IgE class switch), IL-5 (eosinophil activation), and IL-13. The primary driver of Type I hypersensitivity (allergy/asthma).
Suppresses immunity via IL-10, TGF-β, and CTLA-4 contact. FoxP3 mutation causes IPEX syndrome (lethal multi-organ autoimmunity in infant boys).
AID enzyme alters heavy chains. T-cell help (CD40L) is required for memory and switching. BTK mutation causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia (no mature B cells).
IgM (pentamer, immediate complement activator), IgG (most abundant, crosses placenta), IgA (dimer, mucosal), IgE (mast cell bound, allergies).
Recognizes antigens on MHC I. Kills via perforin (pores) + granzyme B (apoptosis). PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint exhaustion in tumors.
Lower activation threshold, larger clone size, and tissue-resident persistence (TRM cells). Basis of vaccine immunity and the germinal center reaction.
IL-8: neutrophil by NLRP3 inflammasome. IL-6 drives CRP in liver, elevated in COVID-19. TNF-α drives cachexia and sepsis. Suppressed by IL-10.
Uncontrolled IL-6, IFN-γ, macrophage amplification. In primary HLH, missing lymphocyte perforin prevents CTLs from shutting off the loop.
I: Immediate IgE. II: Antibody-mediated surface cytotoxicity. III: Soluble immune complex depositing in tissues. IV: Delayed cell-activated (48-72h).
Allergen cross-links IgE on mast cells. Preformed histamine causes immediate vasodilation/bronchoconstriction. Epinephrine 1:1000 IM is the only first-line rescue (reverses shock via α1/β1/β2).
Antibodies attack specific cell surfaces. Causes Goodpasture's (anti-GBM), Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia, and Myasthenia Gravis (receptor blockade without direct lysis).
IgG complexes form in blood during antigen excess. They deposit in small vessels (glomeruli, synovium) = complement activation + neutrophil destruction (e.g., SLE, Serum Sickness).
Cell-mediated, no antibodies! CD4+ Th1 cells recognize antigen, secrete IFN-γ, and activate macrophages. Drives contact dermatitis, tuberculin skin test, and Type 1 Diabetes.
Epithelial defect → Th2 dominance (IL-4/IL-5/IL-13). Allergen immunotherapy desensitizes by shifting the response from Th2 to Treg and inducing IgG4 blocking antibodies.
Activation releases preformed histamine (minutes). Newly synthesized leukotrienes (hours later) cause bronchoconstriction 1000x more potent than histamine. Blocked by montelukast.
Releases Major Basic Protein (MBP) to kill helminths. Driven by IL-5 (Blocked therapeutically by mepolizumab). Causes tissue remodeling in asthma and Hypereosinophilic Syndrome.
Defective apoptotic cell clearance exposes nuclear antigens. TLR9/TLR7 activate Type I IFN and autoantibody production. Treat all patients with hydroxychloroquine.
Synovial inflammation drives invasive pannus formation → cartilage/bone erosion. Anti-CCP antibodies (ACPA) are highly specific. Synovial fluid is neutrophil-rich with low glucose.
Lymphocytic infiltration destroys salivary/lacrimal glands (anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB). Causes extreme xerostomia/dry eyes, and can cause Type 1 Renal Tubular Acidosis.
Endothelial injury → Raynaud's → TGF-β driven fibrosis. Diffuse (anti-Scl-70, early ILD) vs. Limited (anti-centromere). Renal crisis MUST be treated with ACE inhibitors despite AKI.
Polymyositis: CD8+ CTLs destroy muscle expressing aberrant MHC I. Dermatomyositis: Type I IFN drives microangiopathy (Gottron's papules, heliotrope rash). Anti-Jo-1 = antisynthetase syndrome.
Large (Giant Cell Arteritis = blindness risk, immediate steroids). Medium (PAN, Kawasaki). Small (ANCA-associated: GPA/Wegener's = PR3; MPA = MPO).
HLA-B27 misfolding triggers the IL-23/IL-17 axis. Causes AS, Psoriatic, Reactive (can't see, pee, climb a tree), and IBD-arthritis. Sacroiliitis and enthesitis are hallmarks.
Hashimoto's: Th1-mediated destruction → hypothyroidism. Graves' IgG mimics TSH, continually activating the receptor → hyperthyroidism and proptosis (orbital fibroblasts express TSH-R).
CD8+ T cell-mediated destruction of beta cells. Anti-GAD65/IA-2 are markers, not the pathogenic drivers. Teplizumab (anti-CD3) can delay clinical onset in high-risk patients.
IgG antibodies directly attack the GBM/alveolar membrane. Causes pulmonary hemorrhage + Rapidly Progressive GN. Immunofluorescence shows smooth, LINEAR IgG deposition.
Complete failure of T-cell development (and often B/NK cells). Fatal if given live vaccines (e.g., BCG-fatal). Maternal T-cells crossing the placenta can cause fatal GVHD in the infant.
Pro-B fails to transition to pre-B. No mature B cells, no tonsils, no germinal centers. Highly susceptible to encapsulated bacteria (pneumococcus, H. influenzae) after maternal IgG fades at 6 months.

Normal B-cell numbers but defective antibody production (low IgG/IgA). Paradoxically presents with recurrent sinopulmonary infections, severe autoimmunity (cytopenias), and highly increased lymphoma risk.
MAC deficiency (C5-C9) specifically predisposes to meningococcal/gonococcal infections. C1-INH deficiency causes bradykinin-driven hereditary angioedema (unresponsive to epinephrine).
Hyperacute rejection is driven by preformed donor-specific antibodies (prevented by crossmatching). GVHD occurs when donor T-cells attack recipient tissues (skin, gut, liver).
Bind cyclophilin/FKBP12 → inhibit calcineurin → block NFAT dephosphorylation → prevent IL-2 transcription. Highly nephrotoxic (afferent arteriolar constriction).
Binds FKBP12 to inhibit mTOR. Blocks IL-2-driven T-cell proliferation (not production). Non-nephrotoxic. Impairs wound healing, used post-transplant and for CAR-[T].
Inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH). Selectively starves T and B cells, which uniquely rely entirely on de novo purine synthesis and lack a salvage pathway. Teratogenic.
Blocks TNF-α signaling. Highly effective for RA and IBD. Because TNF maintains granulomas, blockade risks fatal reactivation of latent TB. (Etanercept is a decoy receptor, fails in IBD).
Anti-CTLA-4 (Ipilimumab) and anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab) remove inhibitory brakes on T-cells to fight tumors. Causes severe immune-related adverse events (irAEs) like colitis and pneumonitis.
Blocks intracellular JAK-STAT signaling, silencing dozens of cytokine signals simultaneously. Causes high risk of Varicella Zoster (shingles) reactivation—check immunity before starting.
IL-17 (from Th17) drives psoriasis and ankylosing spondylitis (axSpA). Anti-IL-17A is effective in skin/joints but worsens Inflammatory Bowel Disease because IL-17 is protective in the GI mucosa.
Apoptosis is clean. Necrosis is inflammatory. Coagulative necrosis (ischemia) leaves ghost outlines. Liquefactive necrosis (brain/abscesses) causes enzymatic self-digestion.
Death that shouts. Pyroptosis: inflammasome → caspase-1 → IL-1β release via gasdermin pores. Gain-of-function NLRP3 mutations cause CAPS (treat with anakinra).
Persistent TGF-β signaling activates Smad2/3 → fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition → excessive architectural collagen (e.g., IPF, Cirrhosis). Pirfenidone blocks this pathway.
Hallmarks include immune evasion, replicative immortality, and the Warburg effect (aerobic glycolysis). Tumors actively recruit M2 macrophages and Tregs to suppress the local immune response.
The ultimate quest: Every drug, mechanism, and pathology card interacts. If you give Anti-TNF to a RA patient, you disable Granny Granuloma. If you lack BTK, you lose Barb B-Cell.

Anti-TNF (Infliximab/Adalimumab): TNF-α → RA, Crohn's, Psoriasis | Reactivates TB. JAK Inhibitor (Tofacitinib): JAK-STAT → RA, UC | Shingles (VZV) Reactivation. Anti-IL-17 (Secukinumab): IL-17A → Ankylosing Spondylitis | Worsens IBD. Anti-IL-4Rα (Dupilumab): Th2 Axis → Asthma, Atopic Derm | Eosinophilia (transient).
